_comment: Copy this file to eol_config.json and edit to match your stack.
Each product entry has a 'source' field selecting the data provider.
If 'source' is omitted it defaults to 'endoflife_date'.
Supported sources:
endoflife_date   - community endoflife.date API (default)
fields: product, version, label
browse https://endoflife.date/ for product names
and run  curl https://endoflife.date/api/{product}.json
to see valid cycles.
aws_rds_scrape   - scrapes AWS release-calendar docs for RDS / Aurora
minor-version EOL (which endoflife.date doesn't track).
fields: engine, version, label
supported engines: 'aurora-postgresql', 'rds-postgresql'
notify_when: 'always'      = daily report regardless of alerts
'alerts_only' = only when something is EOL or approaching
policy_note (optional, any entry): a short ASCII observation shown as a report
sub-line -- use for no-EOL-date platform/infra (nginx, Tomcat, PuTTY, ...).
notifications: list of output channels. Supported types:
console   - print plain-text report to stdout
html_file - write HTML report to 'path' (a UTC timestamp is inserted
before the extension; default base: eol_report.html)
sns       - publish plain-text to SNS topic. Resolution order:
notif.topic_arn  >  event.sns_topic_arn  >  SNS_TOPIC_ARN env var.
In multi-project deploys the topic ARN is supplied per-invocation
by EventBridge so each project routes to its own topic.
ses       - send HTML email via SES (from_email, to_emails, or env vars;
to_emails / from_email can also come from event payload)

products.label: Nginx 1.29
products.policy_note: nginx cuts a new stable branch about yearly; once a newer stable branch ships the previous one stops getting updates, so an old branch is effectively EOL with no published date.
